verses.zh: 于是以色列从但到别是巴，以及住基列地的众人都出来，如同一人，聚集在米斯巴耶和华面前。
verses.en: All the Israelites from Dan to Beer Sheba[NOTE:1] and from the land of Gilead[NOTE:2] left their homes[NOTE:3] and assembled together[NOTE:4] before the Lord at Mizpah.
notes: Dan was located in the far north of the country, while Beer Sheba was located in the far south. This encompassed all the territory of the land of Canaan occupied by the Israelites.
The land of Gilead was on the eastern side of the Jordan River.
Heb “went out.”
Heb “and the assembly was convened as one man.”
verses.commentary:
20:1 "from Dan to Beersheba" This became an idiom for all the land given to the tribes of Israel. The new
city of Dan (formerly Laish, Judges 18) to Beersheba, a city in the far south (cf. 1 Sam. 3:20; 2 Sam. 17:11; 24:2, 15).

The exact boundaries of the Promised Land are rather ambiguous (NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 803).

- Num. 34:1-12

- Deut. 1:6-8

- Deut. 3:12-26

- Deut. 11:24

- Joshua 1:3-4

- Jos. 13:8-12 (east of Jordan)

- Jdgs. 20:1

This implies a later date than Judges 17-28, but the united action of the tribes (cf. Jdgs. 20:1, 2, 11), the
presence of the ark, and Phinehas, the High Priest in charge (cf. Jdgs. 20:26-28), all point to an early date in the period of
the Judges. Even possibly before Judges 17-18, because the OT historical narratives are not always in chronological order.
Judges was compiled by a later editor during David's reign.

▣ "the land of Gilead" This phrase was used to describe the land (and tribes) east of the Jordan River.
This statement is surprising in light of Jdgs. 21:8-9, which informs us that not all Gilead came to Mizpah.

The VERB "come up" (BDB 748, KB 828, Qal PERFECT,
cf. Jdgs. 21:5, 8) may be idiomatic for meeting YHWH at a worship gathering (NIDOTTE, vol. 2, p. 404).

▣ "the congregation assembled" Israel collectively was called

- the congregation ‒ BDB 417, Jdgs. 20:1

- the assembly ‒ BDB 874, Jdgs. 20:2

The early church chose #2, as translated by the LXX, to refer to themselves. They saw themselves as
the fulfillment of God's promises to Israel. Remember, the writers of the NT (except Luke, who was still influenced by Paul)
were Hebrew thinkers, writing in street Greek (Koine). The best way to understand NT Greek terms is not a Greek lexicon
but the Septuagint.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHURCH (ekklesia)

SPECIAL TOPIC: GREEK GRAMMATICAL TERMS

▣ "Mizpah" Mizpah (BDB 859) means "watchtower" or "outlook point." There are several sites by this
name. This gathering site, about three and a half miles south of Bethel (Jdgs. 20:26-28), is also mentioned in
1 Sam. 7:5-6, 16; 10:17. See The MacMillan Bible Atlas, map #81.

Josephus (Antiq. 5.2.9) says they gathered at "Shiloh" (cf. Jdgs. 18:31). The ark is located at Shiloh
in 1 Sam. 1:3.

verses.zh: 以色列民的首领，就是各支派的军长，都站在　神百姓的会中；拿刀的步兵共有四十万。
verses.en: The leaders[NOTE:1] of all the people from all the tribes of Israel took their places in the assembly of God’s people, which numbered[NOTE:2] 400,000 sword-wielding foot soldiers.
notes: Heb “the cornerstones”; or “the supports.” The word is used of leaders in only three other texts—1 Sam 14:38; Isa 19:13; Zech 10:4.
The words “which numbered” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
verses.commentary:
20:2 "chiefs" This is the Hebrew word for "corner" (BDB 819, #2), used in the sense of "leader" (lit. "cornerstones
of the people"; cf. 1 Sam. 14:38; Isa. 19:13; Zech. 10:4. This becomes imagery for the Messiah.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CORNERSTONE

▣ "400,000" There are several large numbers in this chapter. They do not all add up to the precise total.

Remember,

- it is difficult to translate Hebrew numbers correctly

- the term "thousand" is used in several senses

- round numbers were often used to convey more than just an accurate number of people

SPECIAL TOPIC: THOUSAND (eleph)

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE

verses.zh: 以色列人上到米斯巴，便雅悯人都听见了。以色列人说：「请你将这件恶事的情由对我们说明。」
verses.en: The Benjaminites heard that the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah. Then the Israelites said, “Explain how this wicked thing happened!”
verses.commentary: 20:3-7 The tribes want to hear the story firsthand from the Levite. This is a brief repetition of Judges 19.

verses.zh: 那利未人，就是被害之妇人的丈夫，回答说：「我和我的妾到了便雅悯的基比亚住宿。
verses.en: The Levite,[NOTE:1] the husband of the murdered woman, spoke up, “I and my concubine stopped in[NOTE:2] Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin[NOTE:3] to spend the night.
notes: Heb “The man, the Levite.”
Heb “came to.”
Heb “which belongs to Benjamin.”

verses.zh: 基比亚人夜间起来，围了我住的房子，想要杀我，又将我的妾强奸致死。
verses.en: The leaders of Gibeah attacked me and at night surrounded the house where I was staying.[NOTE:1] They wanted to kill me; instead they abused my concubine so badly that she died.
notes: Heb “arose against me and surrounded against me the house at night.”
verses.commentary:
20:5 "because of me" Josephus says it was because his concubine was beautiful but here the homosexual
intent of the mob is made clear.

The Levite clearly thought the homosexual rape would have killed him (as it did his concubine).

verses.zh: 我就把我妾的尸身切成块子，使人拿着传送以色列得为业的全地，因为基比亚人在以色列中行了凶淫丑恶的事。
verses.en: I took hold of my concubine and carved her up and sent the pieces[NOTE:1] throughout the territory occupied by Israel[NOTE:2] because they committed such an unthinkable atrocity[NOTE:3] in Israel.
notes: Heb “her”; the referent is more naturally stated in English as “the pieces.”
Heb “throughout all the territory of the inheritance of Israel.”
Heb “a wicked and disgraceful [thing].”
verses.commentary: 20:6 See note in Contextual Insights, C.

verses.zh: 你们以色列人都当筹划商议。」
verses.en: All you Israelites,[NOTE:1] make a decision here!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Look, all of you sons of Israel.”
Heb “give for yourselves a word and advice here.”
verses.commentary:
20:7 The Levite asks (BDB 396, KB 393, Qal IMPERATIVE) for

- advice ‒ BDB 182

- counsel ‒ BDB 420

Notice how other translations handle the implication of this IMPERATIVE.

- JPSOA ‒ "Now you are all Israelites; produce a plan of action here and now."

- NJB ‒ "Now, all you Israelites, discuss the matter and give your decision here and now."

verses.zh: 众民都起来如同一人，说：「我们连一人都不回自己帐棚、自己房屋去。
verses.en: All Israel rose up in unison[NOTE:1] and said, “Not one of us will go home![NOTE:2] Not one of us will return[NOTE:3] to his house!
notes: Heb “as one man.”
Heb “to his tent.”
Or “turn aside.”
verses.commentary:
20:8 "all the people arose as one man" This tribal unity is surprising during the period of the Judges
(cf. Jdgs. 20:2, 8, 11). Note some of the tension expressed in Jdgs. 5:15-17; 8:1-3; 12:1-6. Many scholars think
this emphasis on unity was the work of a later editor during David's day. During the period of the judges, there was
only a loose, often regional, cooperation between the tribes. Unity came only with a king.

▣ "his tent. . .his house" It is possible to see these as

- some lived in tents and some in houses

- "tents" is an anachronism

- just literary variety for the same thought

verses.zh: 我们向基比亚人必这样行，照所掣的签去攻击他们。
verses.en: Now this is what we will do to Gibeah: We will attack the city as the lot dictates.[NOTE:1]
notes: As the lot dictates. The Israelite soldiers intended to cast lots to determine which tribe would lead the battle charge (see v. 18).tn Heb “against her by lot.” The verb “we will go up” (נַעֲלֶה, naʿaleh) has probably been accidentally omitted before “against her” (עָלֶיהָ, ʿaleha).
verses.commentary:
20:9 "by lot" This was a means of knowing YHWH's will in a matter (i.e., Jonah 1:7; Acts 1:26). In Jdgs. 20:26-28
Israel consults with the High Priest.

SPECIAL TOPIC: URIM AND THUMMIM

verses.zh: 我们要在以色列各支派中，一百人挑取十人，一千人挑取百人，一万人挑取千人，为民运粮，等大众到了便雅悯的基比亚，就照基比亚人在以色列中所行的丑事征伐他们。」
verses.en: We will take ten of every group of a hundred men from all the tribes of Israel (and a hundred of every group of a thousand, and a thousand of every group of ten thousand) to get supplies for the army.[NOTE:1] When they arrive in Gibeah of Benjamin, they will punish them for the atrocity that they committed in Israel.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “people.”
Heb “to do at their arrival in Geba of Benjamin according to all the disgraceful [thing] which he [collective = “Benjamin”] did in Israel.” Here “Geba” must be an error for “Gibeah.”
verses.commentary:
20:10 This is a practical verse that details how the troops will be supplied.

▣ "to Gibeah" The MT has "Geba" (BDB 148, cf. Jdgs. 20:33; Jos. 18:24; 21:17), but in Jdgs. 19:12;
20:31, it is "Gibeah" (BDB 149 II).

Notice the combined army of Israel was only going to attack Gibeah (Jdgs. 20:11) but in 20:14 all
Benjamin assembled to resist them (Jdgs. 20:14).

verses.zh: 于是以色列众人彼此连合如同一人，聚集攻击那城。
verses.en: So all the men of Israel gathered together at the city as allies.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “gathered at the city as one man, united.”

verses.zh: 以色列众支派打发人去，问便雅悯支派的各家说：「你们中间怎么做了这样的恶事呢？
verses.en: The tribes of Israel sent men throughout the tribe[NOTE:1] of Benjamin, saying, “How could such a wicked thing take place?[NOTE:2]
notes: The MT reads the plural, but surely the singular (which is supported by the LXX and Vulgate) is preferable here.
Heb “What is this wicked thing which happened among you?”
verses.commentary:
20:12-13 The united Israeli army asked the tribe of Benjamin to turn over "the worthless fellows" for
execution but Benjamin, for whatever reason, would not (possibly tribal pride).

verses.zh: 现在你们要将基比亚的那些匪徒交出来，我们好治死他们，从以色列中除掉这恶。」便雅悯人却不肯听从他们弟兄以色列人的话。
verses.en: Now, hand over the good-for-nothings[NOTE:1] in Gibeah, so we can execute them and purge Israel of wickedness.”[NOTE:2] But the Benjaminites refused to listen to their Israelite brothers.
notes: Heb “the men, sons of wickedness.”
Heb “and burn away wickedness from Israel.”

verses.zh: 便雅悯人从他们的各城里出来，聚集到了基比亚，要与以色列人打仗。
verses.en: The Benjaminites came from their cities and assembled at Gibeah[NOTE:1] to make war against the Israelites.
notes: Heb “assembled from the cities at Gibeah.”

verses.zh: 那时便雅悯人从各城里点出拿刀的，共有二万六千；另外还有基比亚人点出七百精兵。
verses.en: That day the Benjaminites mustered from their cities 26,000 sword-wielding soldiers, besides 700 well-trained soldiers from Gibeah.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “besides from the ones living in Gibeah they mustered 700 choice men.”
verses.commentary:
20:15 "26,000" This is the total number of Benjamin's troops plus the 700 from Gibeah. But the numbers
do not add up. Notice

- total 26,700, Jdgs. 20:15 (LXXA, 25,700; LXXB, 23,700)

- those killed

- 22,000 ‒ Jdgs. 20:21, of Israel

- 8,000 ‒ Jdgs. 20:25, of Israel

- 25,100 ‒ Jdgs. 20:35, of Benjamin

- 18,000 ‒ Jdgs. 20:44, of Benjamin

- 2,000 ‒ Jdgs. 20:45, of Benjamin

- only 600 left ‒ Jdgs. 20:47, but what of the 3,000 in Jdgs. 20:45 who were captured not killed?

verses.zh: 在众军之中有拣选的七百精兵，都是左手便利的，能用机弦甩石打人，毫发不差。
verses.en: Among this army[NOTE:1] were 700 specially trained left-handed[NOTE:2] soldiers.[NOTE:3] Each one could sling a stone and hit even the smallest target.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “And from all this people.”
Heb “700 choice men, bound/restricted in the right hand.” On the significance of the idiom, “bound/restricted in the right hand,” see the translator’s note on 3:15.
“at a single hair and not miss.”
Heb “a man of war.”
verses.commentary:
20:16 "left handed" This was unusual (lit. "bound [BDB 32] on the right [BDB 411] hand" [BDB 383]),
which shows that most people were right handed. This phrase always relates to Benjamite warriors (cf.
Jdgs. 3:15 and 1 Chr. 12:2). They were very accurate with the sling. This is ironic because the name
"Benjamin" (BDB 122) means "son of the right hand."

verses.zh: 便雅悯人之外，点出以色列人拿刀的，共有四十万，都是战士。
verses.en: The men of Israel (not counting Benjamin) had mustered 400,000 sword-wielding soldiers, every one an experienced warrior.[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.

verses.zh: 以色列人就起来，到伯特利去求问　神说：「我们中间谁当首先上去与便雅悯人争战呢？」耶和华说：「犹大当先上去。」
verses.en: The Israelites went up to Bethel[NOTE:1] and asked God,[NOTE:2] “Who should lead the charge against the Benjaminites?”[NOTE:3] The Lord said, “Judah should lead.”
notes: Heb “They arose and went up to Bethel and asked God, and the Israelites said.”
Heb “Who should go up for us first for battle against the sons of Benjamin?”
Heb “encamped.”
verses.commentary:
20:18 "Bethel" This was the location of the ark at this period (cf. Jdgs. 20:26-28).

▣ "inquired of God" This would involve asking a priest (cf. Jdgs. 20:18, 23, 27; the first two gatherings
may have taken place at Mizpah). Here the High Priest would either

- use the Urim and Thummim (NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 329-330)

- receive a direct revelation

Notice the term "God" (Elohim) is parallel to YHWH. This parallelism also occurs in Exod. 3:2-12, where

- the angel of YHWH

- Elohim

- YHWH

all appear in a unified context. I do not think this reflects multiple sources , but either

- literary variety

- the specialized connotation of the different names for Deity in Israel

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C. and D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PENTATEUCH SOURCE CRITICISM

▣ "Judah shall go up first" Judges is written to clearly demonstrate the need for a righteous king. It was
probably written during the reign of David, who was from the tribe of Judah (cf. Gen. 49:10). The appendix
to Judges (chapters 17-21) highlights the sins of Benjamin, which was the tribe of Saul, the first king.

By YHWH choosing Judah to go first (as during the exodus), He was establishing their priority.

This phrase has no VERBAL but functions as an IMPERATIVE.

verses.zh: 以色列人早晨起来，对着基比亚安营。
verses.en: The Israelites got up the next morning and moved[NOTE:1] against Gibeah.
notes: Heb “the men of Israel.” The noun phrase has been replaced by the pronoun (“they”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
20:19-28 These verses document the Israeli army's two defeats. This is surprising because they had sought
YHWH's will at the tabernacle in Bethel and it received His blessing.

YHWH tells them to attack three times (Jdgs. 20:18, 23, 28). The unexpected defeats by a much smaller
group (i.e., Benjamin's military) can be seen in Jdgs. 20:23, 26.

- 22,000 of Israel are killed in 20:21

- 18,000 of Israel are killed in 20:25

One wonders if Mizpah was not an approved worship site and only when Israel came to the tabernacle
and ark at Bethel did YHWH honor their request. But this is just speculation. The Jewish Study Bible, p. 552, says, "On the
first two days Israel was defeated, for reasons that are not clear."

Remember, this is not western, chronological, cause-and-effect history. This is history recorded for
theological purposes. Usually several chapters are involved in making the main point (i.e., this was a period of confusion
and evil in Israel's history; they needed a righteous king who would uphold and honor the Mosaic covenant (i.e., David).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE OLD TESTAMENT AS HISTORY

verses.zh: 以色列人出来，要与便雅悯人打仗，就在基比亚前摆阵。
verses.en: The men of Israel marched out to fight Benjamin; they[NOTE:1] arranged their battle lines against Gibeah.
notes: Heb “The sons of Benjamin came out of Gibeah and they struck down in Israel that day 22,000 men to the ground.”

verses.zh: 便雅悯人就从基比亚出来，当日杀死以色列人二万二千。
verses.en: The Benjaminites attacked from Gibeah and struck down 22,000 Israelites that day.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “The people, the men of Israel.”
verses.commentary:
20:21 "20,000" Again, the true number is hard to know.

- the use of round numbers

- the different connotations of "thousand"

verses.zh: 以色列人彼此奋勇，仍在头一日摆阵的地方又摆阵。
verses.en: The Israelite army[NOTE:1] took heart[NOTE:2] and once more arranged their battle lines, in the same place where they had taken their positions the day before.
notes: Or “encouraged one another.”
Heb “I” (collective singular).
verses.commentary:
20:22-23 Many scholars and translations believe these verses have been transposed; Jdgs. 20:23 should
come first.

verses.zh: 未摆阵之先，以色列人上去，在耶和华面前哭号，直到晚上，求问耶和华说：「我们再去与我们弟兄便雅悯人打仗可以不可以？」耶和华说：「可以上去攻击他们。」
verses.en: The Israelites went up and wept before the Lord until evening. They asked the Lord, “Should we[NOTE:1] again march out to fight[NOTE:2] the Benjaminites, our brothers?”[NOTE:3] The Lord said, “Attack them.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “approach for battle.”
Heb “my brother” (collective singular).
Heb “Go up against him” (collective singular).
Heb “drew near to.”

verses.zh: 第二日，以色列人就上前攻击便雅悯人。
verses.en: So the Israelites marched toward[NOTE:1] the Benjaminites the next day.
notes: Heb “And Benjamin went out to meet them from Gibeah the second day, and they again struck down among the sons of Israel 18,000 men to the ground, all of these were wielding the sword.”

verses.zh: 便雅悯人也在这日从基比亚出来，与以色列人接战，又杀死他们一万八千，都是拿刀的。
verses.en: The Benjaminites again attacked them from Gibeah and struck down 18,000 sword-wielding Israelite soldiers.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and all the people.”

verses.zh: 以色列众人就上到伯特利，坐在耶和华面前哭号，当日禁食直到晚上；又在耶和华面前献燔祭和平安祭。
verses.en: So all the Israelites, the whole army,[NOTE:1] went up to[NOTE:2] Bethel.[NOTE:3] They wept and sat there before the Lord; they did not eat anything[NOTE:4] that day until evening. They offered up burnt sacrifices and tokens of peace[NOTE:5] to the Lord.
notes: Heb “went up and came [to].”
For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.
Traditionally, “fasted.”
Or “peace offerings.”
Heb “standing before him.”
verses.commentary:
20:26 "Bethel" This worship site called Bethel in central Canaan (Luz, Gen. 28:19) has two possible origins.

- the vision of Jacob about a ladder reaching from earth to heaven with angels ascending and descending (cf. Gen. 28:10-19)

- the place where Jacob wrestled with the angel and his name was changed to Israel (cf. Gen. 35:5, 9-15)

The location of the tabernacle with the ark was moved several times during the period from Joshua to David
(i.e., Gilgal, Shechem, Shiloh, Bethel, Shiloh, Jerusalem).

▣ "fasting" There are two other places in the OT where Israel fasted in preparation for a battle
(cf. 1 Sam. 7:6; 2 Chr. 20:1-4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

verses.zh: 那时，　神的约柜在那里；亚伦的孙子、以利亚撒的儿子非尼哈侍立在约柜前。以色列人问耶和华说：「我们当再出去与我们弟兄便雅悯人打仗呢？还是罢兵呢？」耶和华说：「你们当上去，因为明日我必将他们交在你们手中。」
verses.en: The Israelites asked the Lord (for the ark of God’s covenant was there in those days;
verses.commentary:
20:27 "the ark of the covenant" This is the only mention of the ark in Judges.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT

verses.zh: a
verses.en: Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, was serving the Lord[NOTE:1] in those days), “Should we[NOTE:2] once more march out to fight the Benjaminites our brothers,[NOTE:3] or should we[NOTE:4] quit?” The Lord said, “Attack, for tomorrow I will hand them[NOTE:5] over to you.”
notes: Heb “I” (collective singular).
Heb “my brother” (collective singular).
Heb “I” (collective singular).
Heb “him” (collective singular).
Heb “the third day.”
verses.commentary:
20:28 "Phinehas" This is an Egyptian name meaning "dark skinned child" or "Negro" (BDB 810). He was
a very loyal priest (cf. Numbers 25) and High Priest (cf. Num. 31:6; Jos. 22:13).

20:28-35 The Israeli army used the same military tactic (i.e., ambush) used by Joshua at Ai (cf. Jos. 8:3-28).
There are several ambushes mentioned in Judges.

- Gideon against Midian ‒ Jdgs. 8:4-12

- men of Shechem against Abimelech ‒ Jdgs. 9:25, 32, 43

- Philistines against Samson ‒ Jdgs. 16:2

- Israeli army against the men of Benjamin ‒ Jdgs. 20:29-48

- remnant of Benjamin against the women of Shiloh ‒ Jdgs. 21:19-23

20:33-36a The NET Bible suggests that Jdgs. 20:33-36a contains a "condensed account of the battle," while
20:36b-48 has a more detailed account. If true, this would help reconcile the differing numbers of troops killed and those
who escaped.

verses.zh: 以色列人在基比亚的四围设下伏兵。
verses.en: So Israel hid men in ambush outside Gibeah.

verses.zh: 第三日，以色列人又上去攻击便雅悯人，在基比亚前摆阵，与前两次一样。
verses.en: The Israelites attacked the Benjaminites the next day;[NOTE:1] they took their positions against Gibeah just as they had done before.
notes: Heb “went out to meet.”

verses.zh: 便雅悯人也出来迎敌，就被引诱离城；在田间两条路上，一通伯特利，一通基比亚，像前两次，动手杀死以色列人约有三十个。
verses.en: The Benjaminites attacked[NOTE:1] the army, leaving the city unguarded.[NOTE:2] They began to strike down their enemy[NOTE:3] just as they had done before. On the main roads (one leads to Bethel,[NOTE:4] the other to Gibeah) and in the field, they struck down[NOTE:5] about 30 Israelites.
notes: Heb “and they were drawn away from the city.”
Heb “from the army wounded ones.”
For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.
The words “they struck down” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Or “run away.”

verses.zh: 便雅悯人说：「他们仍旧败在我们面前。」但以色列人说：「我们不如逃跑，引诱他们离开城到路上来。」
verses.en: Then the Benjaminites said, “They are defeated just as before.” But the Israelites said, “Let’s retreat[NOTE:1] and lure them[NOTE:2] away from the city into the main roads.”
notes: Heb “him” (collective singular).
Verses 33-36a give a condensed account of the battle from this point on, while vv. 36b-48 offer a more detailed version of how the ambush contributed to Gibeah’s defeat.

verses.zh: 以色列众人都起来，在巴力・他玛摆阵，以色列的伏兵从马利・迦巴埋伏的地方冲上前去。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] All the men of Israel got up from their places and took their positions at Baal Tamar, while the Israelites hiding in ambush jumped out of their places west of Gibeah.
notes: Heb “heavy”; or “severe.”
verses.commentary:
20:33 "Baal-tamar" Ba'al was the male fertility god of the Canaanite pantheon, son of El. He was
worshiped at local shrines (i.e., high places, either manmade or natural).

The location of this particular site is on the road between Gibeah and Bethel (ABD, vol. 1, p. 553).

verses.en: Then 10,000 men, well-trained soldiers from all Israel, made a frontal assault against Gibeah; the battle was fierce.[NOTE:1] But the Benjaminites did not realize that disaster was at their doorstep.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And they did not know that touching against them was disaster.”
Heb “And the sons of Israel struck down in Benjamin that day 25,100 men, all of these wielding the sword.”

20:34

The MT has the PREPOSITION (BDB 617), which is very close to the

verses.zh: 耶和华使以色列人杀败便雅悯人。那日，以色列人杀死便雅悯人二万五千一百，都是拿刀的。
verses.en: The Lord annihilated Benjamin before Israel; the Israelites struck down that day 25,100 sword-wielding Benjaminites.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “gave place to.”
verses.commentary:
20:35 "the Lord struck Benjamin" This is YHWH as Divine Warrior. Roland deVaux,
Ancient Israel (p. 260) has a good list of methods.

- asserted ‒ Jos. 10:14, 42; Jdgs. 20:35

- uses elements of nature ‒ Jos. 10:11; 24:7; Jdgs. 5:20; 1 Sam. 7:10

- threw the enemy into confusion ‒ Jdgs. 4:15; 7:22; 1 Sam. 7:10; 14:20

- sending "divine terror" ‒ 1 Sam. 14:15

verses.zh: 于是便雅悯人知道自己败了。先是以色列人；因为靠着在基比亚前所设的伏兵，就在便雅悯人面前诈败。
verses.en: Then the Benjaminites saw they were defeated.The Israelites retreated before[NOTE:1] Benjamin because they had confidence in the men they had hidden in ambush outside Gibeah.
notes: Heb “hurried and put off [their hiding place].”

verses.zh: 伏兵急忙闯进基比亚，用刀杀死全城的人。
verses.en: The men hiding in ambush made a mad dash[NOTE:1] to Gibeah. They[NOTE:2] attacked[NOTE:3] and put the sword to the entire city.
notes: Heb “the men hiding in ambush.”
Or “deployed.” The verb normally means “to lead” or “to draw.”
Heb “they”; the referent (the men hiding in ambush) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 以色列人预先同伏兵约定在城内放火，以烟气上腾为号。
verses.en: The Israelites and the men hiding in ambush had arranged a signal. When the men hiding in ambush[NOTE:1] sent up a smoke signal from the city,
notes: Heb “turned in the battle.”
verses.commentary:
20:38 The prearranged sign between the Israeli force pretending to flee (i.e., in order to draw out the army
of Benjamin) and the Israeli force which attacked Gibeah, was the city being set on fire. This sign caused both groups
to attack Benjamin, caught between them (Jdgs. 20:41), with no place to retreat.

The MT has the Hiphil IMPERATIVE, "make many" (BDB 915, KB 1176),
which seems to refer to a large fire.

verses.zh: 以色列人临退阵的时候，便雅悯人动手杀死以色列人，约有三十个，就说：「他们仍像前次被我们杀败了。」
verses.en: the Israelites counterattacked.[NOTE:1] Benjamin had begun to strike down the Israelites;[NOTE:2] they struck down[NOTE:3] about 30 men. They said, “There’s no doubt about it! They are totally defeated as in the earlier battle.”
notes: Heb “And Benjamin began to strike down wounded ones among the men of Israel.”
The words “they struck down” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “Benjamin turned after him and, look, the whole city went up toward the sky.”
verses.commentary:
20:39 "Surely they are defeated" This is an intensified Hebrew grammatical feature (i.e., a Niphal
INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and PARTICIPLE of the same root, BDB 619, KB 669).

verses.zh: 当烟气如柱从城中上腾的时候，便雅悯人回头观看，见全城的烟气冲天。
verses.en: But when the signal, a pillar of smoke, began to rise up from the city, the Benjaminites turned around and saw the whole city going up in a cloud of smoke that rose high into the sky.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “were terrified.”

verses.zh: 以色列人又转身回来，便雅悯人就甚惊惶，因为看见灾祸临到自己了。
verses.en: When the Israelites turned around, the Benjaminites panicked[NOTE:1] because they could see that disaster was on their doorstep.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “disaster touched against them.”
Heb “clung to”; or “stuck close.”

verses.zh: 他们在以色列人面前转身往旷野逃跑；以色列人在后面追杀。那从各城里出来的，也都夹攻杀灭他们。
verses.en: They retreated before the Israelites, taking the road to the wilderness. But the battle overtook[NOTE:1] them as men from the surrounding cities struck them down.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and those from the cities were striking them down in their midst.”
The translation assumes the reading מִנּוֹחָה (minnokhah, “from Nohah”; cf. 1 Chr 8:2) rather than the MT’s מְנוּחָה (menukhah, “resting place”).

verses.zh: 以色列人围绕便雅悯人，追赶他们，在他们歇脚之处、对着日出之地的基比亚践踏他们。
verses.en: They surrounded the Benjaminites, chased them from Nohah,[NOTE:1] and annihilated[NOTE:2] them all the way to a spot east of Geba.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “tread down, walk on.”

Heb “unto the opposite of Gibeah toward the east.” Gibeah cannot be correct here, since the Benjaminites retreated from there toward the desert and Rimmon (see v. 45). A slight emendation yields the reading “Geba.”
Heb “they”; the referent (the rest [of the Benjaminites]) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
verses.commentary:
20:43 The Jewish Study Bible, p. 555, calls this verse a "difficult poem," but no English translation,
including JPSOA, shows it indented.

▣

NASB, REB
"without rest"

NRSV, NET, LXXB
"from Nohah"

TEV, LXXA
"without stopping"

NJB
"relentlessly"

JPSOA
"from Menuhah"

The MT has "at their resting place" (BDB 629). The UBS Text Project, p. 130, gives this a "B" rating
(some doubt). There are several suggested emendations following the same basic thought (see pp. 130-131).

The name Nohah appears in 1 Chr. 8:2 as a person's name (i.e., one of Benjamin's sons). So surely
it could have been the name of a region, locality, or town.

verses.zh: 便雅悯人死了的有一万八千，都是勇士。
verses.en: So 18,000 Benjaminites, all of them capable warriors, fell dead.

verses.zh: 其余的人转身向旷野逃跑，往临门磐去。以色列人在道路上杀了他们五千人，如拾取遗穗一样，追到基顿又杀了他们二千人。
verses.en: The rest[NOTE:1] turned and ran toward the wilderness, heading toward the cliff of Rimmon. But the Israelites[NOTE:2] caught[NOTE:3] 5,000 of them on the main roads. They stayed right on their heels[NOTE:4] all the way to Gidom and struck down 2,000 more.
notes: Heb “and they”; the referent (the Israelites) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “gleaned.” The word is an agricultural term which pictures Israelites picking off the Benjaminites as easily as one picks grapes from the vine.
Heb “stuck close after them.”

The number given here (25,000 sword-wielding Benjaminites) is an approximate figure; v. 35 gives the more exact number (25,100). According to v. 15, the Benjaminite army numbered 26,700 (26,000 + 700). The figures in vv. 35 (rounded in vv. 44-46) and 47 add up to 25,700. What happened to the other 1,000 men? The most reasonable explanation is that they were killed during the first two days of fighting. G. F. Moore (Judges [ICC], 429) and C. F. Burney (Judges, 475) reject this proposal, arguing that the narrator is too precise and concerned about details to omit such a fact. However, the account of the first two days’ fighting emphasizes Israel’s humiliating defeat. To speak of Benjaminite casualties would diminish the literary effect. In vv. 35, 44-47 the narrator’s emphasis is the devastating defeat that Benjamin experienced on this final day of battle. To mention the earlier days’ casualties at this point is irrelevant to his literary purpose. He allows readers who happen to be concerned with such details to draw conclusions for themselves.

20:45-47 The numbers through here are uncertain (i.e., Jdgs. 20:45), but the remnant is only 600 men!

verses.en: That day 25,000[NOTE:1] sword-wielding Benjaminites fell in battle, all of them capable warriors.[NOTE:2]

verses.zh: 只剩下六百人，转身向旷野逃跑，到了临门磐，就在那里住了四个月。
verses.en: But 600 survivors turned and ran away to the wilderness, to the cliff of Rimmon. They stayed there four months.
verses.commentary:
20:47 "the rock of Rimmon" This location was about 4 miles west of Bethel (The MacMillan Bible Atlas,
map #86). However, there are several locations which include this name (a Benjamite, cf. 2 Sam. 4:2, 5, 9). Wherever it
was, it was a large rock formation, or possibly a high cave which gave protection to the remnant of Benjamin (ABA, vol. 5,
pp. 173-174).

verses.zh: 以色列人又转到便雅悯地，将各城的人和牲畜，并一切所遇见的，都用刀杀尽，又放火烧了一切城邑。
verses.en: The Israelites returned to the Benjaminite towns[NOTE:1] and put the sword to them. They wiped out the cities,[NOTE:2] the animals, and everything they could find. They set fire to every city in their path.[NOTE:3]
notes: The translation is based on the reading מֵעִיר מְתִים (meʿir metim, “from a city of men,” i.e., “an inhabited city”), rather than the reading מֵעִיר מְתֹם (meʿir metom, “from a city of soundness”) found in the Leningrad Codex (L).
Heb “Also all the cities that were found they set on fire.”
verses.commentary:
20:48 The Holy War techniques used in the conquest are employed against the cities of Benjamin; everything
that breathes dies! Archeology records that Gibeah was destroyed in the mid 12th century B.C.

▣ "all that they found" This may be a Hebrew idiom for "captured people" (cf. Isa. 13:15; 22:3; note
parallelism).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Was Mizpah an approved worship site?

- Why is 400,000 too large a number? If so, how does one deal with it?

- Why did Israel feel they must act against the wickedness of one Benjamite city?

- Why would Benjamin not turn over these "worthless fellows"?

- How does Jdgs. 20:18 fit into the overall purpose of the book?

- Is the worship site at Bethel the location of the tabernacle or was Shiloh?

- Why did the Israeli military destroy all the Benjamite cities and kill their entire population?

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- It is surprising that "all Israel" (Jdgs. 20:1, 2, 11) agreed on anything.

- The disgraceful covenant violation of Benjamin demanded a response. This is similar to Joshua 7:15, 22.

- The acts of the "worthless fellow" (lit. "sons of "Belial") are characterized as

- wickedness ‒ BDB 949, cf. Jdgs. 20:3,12,13 (translated "disaster" in 20:34,41; it is used often in Jeremiah)

- lewd ‒ BDB 273 I, Jdgs. 20:6, cf. 20:44, 48, 49; Ezek. 16:27, 43, 58; 22:9, 21, 27; 23:29, 35, 44, 48, 49

- disgraceful ‒ BDB 615, Jdgs. 19:23; 20:6, 10, 12; Gen. 34:7; Deut. 22:21; 2 Sam. 13:12; Jer. 29:23 (all with
sexually inappropriate acts)

God's people are to live their lives within covenant guidelines which encourage and support long
term societal stability, not instant personal gratification!

- This slaughter of Benjamin was sanctioned by YHWH (cf. Jdgs. 20:17, 23, 26-28). There are consequences to choices
(cf. Gal. 6:7),

- individually (the worthless fellows)

- corporately (the tribe of Benjamin refusing YHWH's words)

- corporately (the sadness of all Israel about what they have done)
